selected_hotel.name: Golden Circle & Southern Highlands, Iceland Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote highland areas.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel, and one drink.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot pools. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and offers a more local experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik while sampling iconic Icelandic foods including skyr, lamb soup, fresh-caught Arctic char, and traditional rye bread baked in geothermal ground. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and learn about Norse mythology and Viking heritage from a local guide.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The water is filtered through lava rock for decades, making it among the clearest on Earth. A truly once-in-a-lifetime geological and aquatic adventure.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Southern Highlands, Iceland Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Flybus or shared shuttle to Reykjavik (~45 min, ~3,500 ISK). Check into a budget hostel or guesthouse in Reykjavik for the first night before heading to Golden Circle area tomorrow. Grab a quick orientation walk around the city center near Hallgrimskirkja church.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Reykjavik city center for a self-guided evening walk. Visit Harpa Concert Hall (free exterior viewing) and stroll along the waterfront. Watch for northern lights if skies clear — the city outskirts offer decent viewing. Check aurora forecast apps (Vedur.is) for alerts.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at Keflavik Airport (bring your own food to save money)
meals.lunch: Grab a hot dog at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur in Reykjavik — Iceland's most famous budget meal (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Supermarket dinner from Bonus or Kronan supermarket — pick up skyr, bread, cheese, and ready meals (~1,500 ISK total)

day_by_day.notes: January in Iceland means very short daylight hours (around 5-6 hours of daylight). Sunrise around 11:00, sunset around 16:00. Bundle up — temperatures typically range from -5°C to 4°C. Purchase a local SIM card at the airport for data access to aurora and weather apps. Stock up on groceries at the airport Bonus supermarket to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, check out and travel to the Golden Circle & Southern Highlands accommodation. Stop en route at Þingvellir National Park (free entry) — walk the Almannagjá gorge, where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Explore the historic Alþingi parliament site and crystal-clear Silfra fissure viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the famous Geysir Geothermal Area (free entry). Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes — a spectacular and completely free natural show. Walk the geothermal field trails and observe boiling mud pools and steaming vents. Visit the nearby Gullfoss waterfall (free entry) — one of Iceland's most iconic two-tiered waterfalls, especially dramatic in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Check into the Golden Circle & Southern Highlands boutique stay. Settle in and warm up. After dinner, head out to a dark area near the accommodation for northern lights hunting — January offers excellent aurora chances with long dark nights. Set an alarm for midnight for a second viewing attempt if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at Reykjavik accommodation or pack food from the supermarket the night before — bread, skyr, and fruit (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Þingvellir or Geysir area — sandwiches and thermos of hot coffee/tea prepared in the morning (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the boutique stay if kitchen facilities are available — pasta with canned tomato sauce and local lamb meatballs from supermarket (~1,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Þingvellir, Geysir, and Gullfoss are all free to enter — the Golden Circle's main attractions cost nothing. Rent a car if not already arranged — essential for this region. Budget car rentals start around 8,000-12,000 ISK/day. Dress in waterproof layers; Gullfoss spray can drench visitors even in winter. Aurora forecast: check vedur.is regularly.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and check aurora forecast from last night's viewing. After breakfast, drive to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — one of Iceland's oldest and most affordable hot springs (~3,000 ISK entry vs. ~7,000+ ISK at Blue Lagoon). Soak in the naturally heated 38-40°C pool surrounded by geothermal activity and small geysers. Perfect budget hot spring experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kerið Volcanic Crater (free or ~400 ISK entry). Walk the rim of this vivid red and green volcanic crater with a serene lake at the bottom. In winter, the crater walls may be dusted with snow creating a stunning contrast. Afterward, explore the small town of Selfoss for a short walk along the Ölfusá river bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Golden Circle accommodation. Spend the evening aurora hunting from the property grounds or drive a few kilometers from any light pollution. January darkness sets in by 16:00, giving maximum aurora viewing time. Bring hot drinks in a thermos for the wait.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal or skyr with berries prepared at the accommodation (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches and fruit eaten in the car or at Kerið crater (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Visit the local Flúðir or Selfoss supermarket and cook a budget meal — grilled lamb chops with potatoes and salad (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic experience. Book in advance during winter as slots can fill up. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees. Kerið Crater is a short detour that adds great variety to the day. Driving distances in this region are manageable — roughly 50-80 km between sites.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the South Coast. Stop at Seljalandsfoss waterfall (free entry, parking fee ~750 ISK). In summer you can walk behind the falls, but in January the path may be icy and closed — check conditions. The waterfall is still stunning from the front with winter ice formations. Continue to nearby Gljúfrabúi hidden waterfall (free, 5-min walk).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss waterfall (free entry). Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views of the South Coast — on clear days you can see the ocean and surrounding mountains. Walk along the river trail if energy allows. Drive further to Dyrhólaey peninsula viewpoint (free) for dramatic coastal views and black sand beach vistas.
day_by_day.evening: Reach the Vík area for a short stop at the famous Reynisfjara black sand beach (free). Observe the basalt column formations and sea stacks (Reynisdrangar) in the fading light. Exercise caution — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous here, even in winter. Return toward Golden Circle area or stay in a Vík guesthouse if budget allows for a shorter drive tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast from accommodation — bread, cheese, boiled eggs, and coffee in a thermos (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Skógafoss — soup in a thermos and sandwiches (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Vík has limited budget options — try the Súður-Vík restaurant or grab groceries from the N1 petrol station convenience store for a simple meal (~1,500-2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast drive is one of Iceland's most scenic routes. In January, roads can be icy — drive slowly and check road conditions at road.is before departing. Seljalandsfoss walkway behind the falls is typically closed in winter due to ice. Reynisfjara beach is genuinely dangerous — never turn your back on the ocean. Total driving: approximately 180-200 km round trip from Golden Circle.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Þórsmörk (Thor's Valley) trailhead area — accessible in winter only with a super jeep or guided tour (budget option: join a shared super jeep tour from ~8,000-12,000 ISK). Alternatively, hike the lower accessible trails near Skógar if Þórsmörk roads are impassable. Explore the dramatic highland valley scenery with glaciers and volcanic mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon (free entry) — a breathtaking 100-meter deep canyon carved by glacial water. The 2 km canyon rim walk offers incredible views. In winter, arrive before 15:00 to make use of daylight. The canyon walls are often coated in moss and ice creating a surreal landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Golden Circle accommodation. This is a great evening for a long aurora watch session — find a hilltop or open field away from any lights. Bring a tripod if you have a camera for long-exposure aurora photography. Hot chocolate and warm blankets are essential.

meals.breakfast: Skyr parfait with granola and honey prepared at accommodation (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed thermos soup and bread rolls eaten at Fjaðrárgljúfur (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook hearty lamb soup (kjötsúpa) at the accommodation using a simple recipe — lamb, potatoes, carrots, and turnips from the supermarket (~1,200 ISK for a large pot)

day_by_day.notes: Þórsmörk is only accessible in winter via specially modified super jeep vehicles — F-roads are closed to regular cars. Check Safetravel.is for current highland road conditions. Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon is free but parking may have a small fee. The canyon rim can be slippery in winter — wear crampons or ice cleats (available cheaply at Bonus or outdoor stores). January aurora probability is high — KP index of 3+ gives visible auroras in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Haukadalur geothermal valley area more deeply — walk the free geothermal trails around the Geysir area that you may have rushed through on Day 2. Visit the Geysir Center museum (free outdoor areas) and photograph the colorful hot spring pools in morning light. The low winter sun creates beautiful golden-hour lighting even at midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths (entry ~3,900 ISK — budget-friendly hot spring option). Soak in the lakeside geothermal pools with views of Lake Laugarvatn. Watch the unique geothermal bakery demonstration where bread is baked underground using geothermal heat. Try a slice of the geothermal rye bread (~500 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation for a relaxed evening. Check aurora forecasts and head out if conditions are favorable. January evenings with clear skies and KP3+ aurora activity can produce spectacular green and purple displays. Stay out until midnight for best chances.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with cinnamon and raisins cooked at accommodation (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Geysir area — thermos soup and crackers with cheese (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta with Icelandic lamb mince sauce — purchase ingredients from Bonus supermarket in Selfoss (~1,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Laugarvatn Fontana is a great mid-budget hot spring option — cheaper than the Blue Lagoon but with a lovely natural setting. The geothermal bread tasting is a unique cultural experience worth the small cost. Laugarvatn town has a small supermarket for resupply. This is a good day to do laundry if the accommodation has facilities — January is cold and wet clothing needs to dry.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Langjökull Glacier area. Drive to the Húsafell area and take a budget snowmobile or glacier walk tour on Langjökull — Iceland's second largest glacier. Budget tour options start around 12,000-15,000 ISK. Alternatively, explore the Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls (free entry) — unique lava field waterfalls where water bubbles up through the lava rock.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Deildartunguhver — Europe's most powerful hot spring (free to view). The boiling water gushes at 180 liters per second at 100°C — an impressive sight. Nearby, explore the ancient Reykholt village and Snorralaug hot spring pool (free viewing), historically used by medieval scholar Snorri Sturluson.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the Golden Circle accommodation. Stop at a dark roadside pullout for northern lights viewing on the way back if skies are clear. The rural roads west of Þingvellir offer excellent dark sky conditions. Hot drinks and warm layers are essential for roadside aurora watching.

meals.breakfast: Scrambled eggs and toast prepared at accommodation (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches and fruit eaten at Hraunfossar waterfalls (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Stop at the Húsafell petrol station for a budget hot meal, or cook at home — grilled fish (Icelandic cod or haddock from supermarket) with boiled potatoes (~1,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hraunfossar and Barnafoss are free and completely unique geological formations — highly recommended. Deildartunguhver is an impressive free natural attraction. The drive to Húsafell from Golden Circle is about 1.5 hours each way — start early to maximize daylight. Langjökull glacier tours should be booked in advance. Check road.is for Route 518 and 550 conditions in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning at the accommodation — catch up on sleep especially if you've been doing late-night aurora watching. Prepare a leisurely breakfast and plan the week ahead. Use the morning to reorganize gear, do laundry, and check weather forecasts for the coming days. Review aurora forecasts for the best upcoming viewing nights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around the Golden Circle accommodation on foot. Walk to nearby farms, fields, and viewpoints. Visit any local geothermal pools or natural hot pots in the immediate area (many are free or very cheap). Look for the small hidden hot pots that locals use — ask accommodation staff for recommendations.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a special budget 'feast' at the accommodation — Icelandic lamb stew with root vegetables, fresh Icelandic bread, and skyr for dessert. Spend the evening stargazing and aurora watching from the accommodation grounds. January nights are long — up to 19 hours of darkness, maximizing aurora opportunities.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at accommodation — eggs, toast, fruit, and coffee (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at accommodation — skyr with fruit and crackers with cheese (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Special home-cooked Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) with fresh bread — all ingredients from Bonus supermarket (~1,800 ISK for a generous meal)

day_by_day.notes: A rest day is important on a 13-day trip, especially in January when outdoor activities are physically demanding. Use this day to recharge physically and mentally. Ask your accommodation hosts about hidden local gems — boutique stay owners often know secret hot pots, viewpoints, and aurora spots that aren't in guidebooks. Check if the accommodation offers any included activities or local tours.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula for a full day exploration. Start at the Bridge Between Continents (free) — a small footbridge spanning the fissure between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Walk across two continents! Continue to the Reykjanesvirkjun geothermal power plant area for dramatic steaming landscape views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gunnuhver mud pools and hot springs (free) — the largest hot spring in Iceland with boiling mud and dramatic steam columns. Visit the Reykjanes Lighthouse (free) at Iceland's most southwesterly point. Walk the dramatic coastal lava fields and sea cliffs. Stop at the Bridge Between Continents area for more geological exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Return via Grindavík town for a supermarket resupply. Check if the Reykjanes area offers good aurora viewing on the way back — the peninsula's dark coastline is excellent for northern lights. Return to Golden Circle accommodation for the night.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast from accommodation — thermos coffee, bread rolls, and cheese (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Gunnuhver or the lighthouse area — packed sandwiches and hot soup (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Fish and chips style meal cooked at home — battered cod with oven fries and coleslaw from supermarket ingredients (~1,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula has seen significant volcanic activity in recent years (2021-2024 eruptions). Check safetravel.is and local news for current volcanic activity and road closures before visiting. The area may have active lava flows or restricted zones. Gunnuhver mud pools are genuinely dangerous — stay strictly on marked paths. The Bridge Between Continents is a quirky and completely free attraction. Driving distance from Golden Circle: approximately 100 km each way.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Þingvellir National Park for a deeper exploration than Day 2. Hike the Hakið viewpoint trail for panoramic views over the rift valley and Lake Þingvallavatn — Iceland's largest natural lake. The 2-3 hour circular hike is free and offers stunning winter scenery. Bring microspikes for icy trail sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Þingvellir church and historic farm buildings (free exterior viewing). Walk the full length of Almannagjá gorge from north to south. Visit the Öxará river and the historic 'drowning pool' (Drekkingarhylur) — a sobering piece of Icelandic history. Stop at the park visitor center for free exhibits about Iceland's geological and historical significance.
day_by_day.evening: Þingvellir is one of Iceland's best aurora viewing locations — minimal light pollution and open skies over the lake. Park at the Hakið viewpoint or Leirar campsite area for aurora watching. The lake reflection can double the visual impact of a strong aurora display. Stay until 23:00 if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Hot oatmeal with brown sugar and dried fruit at accommodation (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Þingvellir — thermos soup, bread, and fruit eaten at a viewpoint bench (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook Icelandic-style baked salmon with dill and lemon at accommodation — salmon is affordable in Icelandic supermarkets (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Þingvellir in winter is magical and far less crowded than summer. The park is free to enter (small parking fee applies). Trail conditions vary — always check with the visitor center about current hiking safety. The lake viewpoints are particularly beautiful when frozen or partially frozen. This is arguably the best aurora viewing spot in the Golden Circle region — the wide open lake provides unobstructed horizon views in all directions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hveragerði geothermal town — known as the 'Hot Spring Town.' Walk the free outdoor geothermal area in the town center where hot springs bubble up through the streets. Visit the NLFI Rehabilitation and Health Clinic geothermal park area (free outdoor access). The town has a unique atmosphere with greenhouses heated by geothermal energy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Reykjadalur Hot Spring River trail from Hveragerði (free). The 6 km round-trip hike leads to a naturally heated river where you can bathe in the hot spring water — completely free! The hike takes 2-3 hours round trip. In winter, the trail can be snowy and icy — bring proper footwear and trekking poles. The contrast of snow-covered hills and steaming hot river is spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation tired but happy from the hike. Warm up with a hot shower and cook dinner. Check aurora forecast — if conditions are good (KP3+, clear skies), bundle up and head out for a late aurora session. The Hveragerði area has good dark sky access just outside town.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast with Icelandic butter and jam at accommodation (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the Reykjadalur hike — energy bars, sandwiches, and hot chocolate in a thermos (~500 ISK). Eat at the hot spring river.
meals.dinner: Simple but satisfying dinner at accommodation — grilled chicken thighs with roasted root vegetables (~1,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur Hot Spring River hike is one of the best FREE hot spring experiences in Iceland. The hike is moderately challenging in winter — the path can be very muddy and icy. Wear waterproof boots and bring a change of clothes for soaking in the river. There are no changing facilities — bring a large towel and change discreetly. The hike is approximately 3 km each way with 200m elevation gain. Start no later than 13:00 in January to return before dark (sunset ~16:00).

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — make the most of it! Drive to Nesjavellir Geothermal Power Plant (free exterior viewing) on the shores of Lake Þingvallavatn. The massive steaming cooling towers against the winter landscape create an otherworldly scene. Drive the scenic Route 360 around the lake for beautiful winter photography opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Úthlíðar and explore the Þingvellir lake shoreline trails (free). Stop at the Silfra fissure viewing area for a final look at the crystal-clear glacial water between the tectonic plates. If budget allows, a snorkeling tour in Silfra is approximately 15,000-18,000 ISK — the water is 2°C year-round but dry suits are provided. Otherwise, enjoy the free viewpoints.
day_by_day.evening: Final aurora hunting night — this is your last best chance! Drive to the darkest spot you've found during the trip. Check vedur.is for the forecast and set multiple alarms throughout the night if the KP index is favorable. Celebrate the trip with a small bottle of Icelandic schnapps (Brennivín, the 'Black Death') from the Vínbúðin state liquor store (~2,500 ISK) enjoyed responsibly while watching the northern lights.

meals.breakfast: Special final-days breakfast — Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) made at accommodation with jam and cream (~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch by the lake — remaining supermarket supplies, cheese, crackers, and fruit (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on the final dinner — visit a local restaurant in Selfoss or Laugarvatn for a budget meal. Try the fish soup (lobster bisque / humarsúpa) which is often affordable at local restaurants (~2,500-3,500 ISK for a full meal with bread)

day_by_day.notes: This is your last full night in Iceland — maximize aurora viewing time. Set alarms for 23:00, 01:00, and 03:00 to check sky conditions. The Þingvellir lake area and any rural hilltop near the accommodation are ideal dark sky locations. Pack bags tonight to make the morning departure smooth. Keep one warm outfit accessible for the morning drive to the airport. Review what's been spent vs. budget — calculate any remaining funds for airport purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake up early and do one last aurora check if you haven't slept yet from a late-night viewing session. Pack all belongings and check out of the Golden Circle accommodation. Drive toward Keflavik Airport (approximately 1-1.5 hours from Golden Circle area). Stop at a roadside viewpoint on the way for one final look at the Icelandic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik Airport with plenty of time before departure. Return rental car if applicable. Browse the duty-free shop for affordable Icelandic souvenirs — Icelandic wool products, skyr candy, licorice, and Brennivín are popular and relatively affordable. The duty-free shop at Keflavik has better prices than city shops for alcohol and chocolate.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of northern lights, hot springs, waterfalls, and glaciers. Review photos and plan the next Iceland adventure — there's always more to explore!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at accommodation using remaining food supplies — keep it simple with bread, cheese, and fruit (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Airport meal — Keflavik Airport has a few budget options. The Pylsur (hot dog) stand is the cheapest option (~600 ISK). Alternatively, bring packed food from accommodation to the airport.
meals.dinner: Meal on the return flight or airport dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours at Keflavik Airport before international flights — security and check-in can take time. The Flybus from Selfoss/Reykjavik to the airport costs ~2,500-4,000 ISK and is the budget alternative to a taxi. Return the rental car with a full tank — fueling at the airport is significantly more expensive than at town petrol stations. Budget summary: a 13-day Iceland trip on a tight budget typically costs 150,000-220,000 ISK (~€1,000-1,500) per person including accommodation, food, transport, and activities when using supermarkets, free attractions, and budget hot springs.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Southern Highlands, Iceland Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel, and one drink.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00 at Keflavík International Airport. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange rental car pickup at the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Keflavík toward the Golden Circle & Southern Highlands accommodation (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Stop at the iconic Öxará River viewpoint near Þingvellir National Park en route to stretch your legs and take in the dramatic winter landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Check into the boutique stay, settle in, and take a short orientation walk around the property. As darkness falls (around 16:00 in January), step outside or ask the hotel staff about the best local spots to watch for the Northern Lights. Clear skies tonight could offer your first sighting.

meals.breakfast: N/A – onboard flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport arrival hall café (sandwiches, soup, coffee) before hitting the road.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nearby local bistro – try Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) and fresh-baked rye bread to warm up after travel.

day_by_day.notes: January daylight in Iceland is very limited (roughly 10:00–16:00). Drive carefully as roads can be icy. Download the Vedur.is weather app and the Aurora Forecast app before leaving the airport. Pick up a road map and check road conditions at road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament, the Alþingi. Stunning frost-covered landscapes in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the famous Geysir Geothermal Area. Watch the Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water up to 40 metres high. Explore the surrounding hot spring fields and fumaroles. Then continue to Gullfoss Waterfall – one of Iceland's most majestic, partially frozen in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay. After dinner, bundle up and head out for Northern Lights hunting. The hotel area away from city light pollution offers excellent aurora viewing conditions.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at the hotel – skyr, eggs, smoked salmon, rye bread, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Warm up at the Geysir Center café with lamb stew or fish chowder and a hot chocolate.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel or a local restaurant – grilled Arctic char with roasted root vegetables and Icelandic butter.

day_by_day.notes: Wear thermal layers and waterproof boots. Þingvellir, Geysir, and Gullfoss form the classic Golden Circle triangle – all within comfortable driving distance. Gullfoss can be very windy; bring a balaclava.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir – Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a wonderfully natural and less commercialized hot spring experience. Soak in 38–40°C geothermal waters surrounded by steaming geysers and snow-dusted fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Flúðir and its surrounding greenhouse farms (some open to visitors in winter). Drive through the scenic Hvítá river valley and stop at Faxi Waterfall – a quieter, beautiful cascade often missed by tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay. Enjoy a cozy evening in – many Icelandic boutique hotels offer hot tubs or outdoor geothermal pools on-site. Check aurora forecast and spend time stargazing or watching for the Northern Lights from the property.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – oatmeal porridge with bilberry jam, Icelandic yogurt, and fresh coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic-style lunch from a local grocery store in Flúðir – Icelandic cheese, flatbread (flatbrauð), smoked lamb, and fruit.
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner at the hotel – slow-roasted lamb shank with mashed turnip and herb sauce, paired with a local Icelandic craft beer.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is far more affordable than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic experience. Book in advance online. Flúðir is a small farming community known for mushroom cultivation and geothermal greenhouses.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the South Coast. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall – walk behind the curtain of water (icy in winter, crampons recommended, available for rent nearby). Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall, one of Iceland's biggest and most photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík – dramatic basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and crashing Atlantic waves. Explore the nearby Dyrhólaey promontory for sweeping coastal views and potential puffin burrow sightings (though puffins are absent in January).
day_by_day.evening: Check into overnight accommodation near Vík or drive back toward the Golden Circle base. If staying south, enjoy dinner in Vík village. Watch for Northern Lights over the black beach – a spectacular backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing.
meals.lunch: Fish and chips or lamb burger at a café near Skógafoss or the Skógar Museum café.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík – known for hearty Icelandic fish dishes and a warm atmosphere. Try pan-seared cod with capers and brown butter.

day_by_day.notes: NEVER turn your back on the ocean at Reynisfjara – sneaker waves are extremely dangerous. Heed all warning signs. Seljalandsfoss path behind the waterfall may be closed due to ice – check locally. Crampons can be rented at nearby farms.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Sólheimajökull glacier – join a guided glacier walk on this accessible tongue of the Mýrdalsjökull ice cap. Crampons and ice axes provided by tour operators. A thrilling and otherworldly winter experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skógar Folk Museum – a fascinating open-air collection of traditional turf houses showcasing Icelandic rural life. Then drive to the Lava Centre in Hvolsvöllur for an immersive exhibition on Iceland's volcanic and seismic activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Golden Circle boutique stay. Relax in the hotel's hot tub or outdoor pool if available. Northern Lights watch from the hotel grounds.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast to prepare for the glacier walk.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or soup at the Skógar Museum café.
meals.dinner: Back at the hotel – enjoy a warming dinner of Icelandic beef stew (plokkfiskur variation) with crusty bread and salad.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sólheimajökull glacier walk in advance through operators like Arcanum or Local Guide. Minimum age and fitness level may apply. Dress in multiple warm layers as glacier winds are biting. The Lava Centre in Hvolsvöllur is excellent for understanding Iceland's geology.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated Blue Lagoon Day. Drive to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa near Grindavík (approx. 1.5 hrs from Golden Circle). Arrive for a morning session – soak in the iconic milky-blue silica-rich geothermal waters, apply the complimentary silica mud mask, and enjoy the algae mask station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your Blue Lagoon experience – enjoy an in-water massage (book in advance), use the steam rooms and sauna, and relax in the warmer inner lagoon areas. The surreal steam rising over the lava fields in winter is magical.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the Golden Circle. Stop in Reykjavík on the way back for a stroll along the Laugavegur shopping street and a peek at Hallgrímskirkja church lit up at night. Head back to the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast before departing early.
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon – splurge slightly on the lagoon-side dining experience. Try the Icelandic langoustine soup or smoked salmon platter.
meals.dinner: Stop in Reykjavík at a mid-range restaurant – try Messinn for exceptional pan-fried fish dishes or Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja for traditional Icelandic food at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon tickets well in advance – they sell out weeks ahead, especially in winter. The Comfort package (mid-range) includes towel, silica mask, algae mask, and one drink. Arrive early to beat crowds. Check road conditions to Grindavík given its proximity to recent volcanic activity zones.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the boutique stay. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and explore the hotel grounds. Many Golden Circle boutique hotels offer yoga, spa treatments, or guided nature walks – inquire with staff.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kerið Volcanic Crater Lake – a stunning crimson and emerald crater lake formed 6,500 years ago. Walk the rim for panoramic views and descend to the lakeside. Nearby, visit the Skálholt Cathedral, Iceland's historic religious center.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights evening excursion. Join a local guided Northern Lights tour departing from the Golden Circle area, or self-drive to a high-altitude dark spot recommended by hotel staff. Bring thermos with hot cocoa.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast – full spread with smoked fish, eggs, pastries, and Icelandic skyr.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café in Selfoss town – soup of the day and a sandwich.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant in Selfoss – try Tryggvaskáli in the historic old town building, serving Icelandic classics with a modern twist.

day_by_day.notes: Kerið is one of the few volcanic craters in Iceland where you can walk to the water's edge. Small entrance fee applies. Skálholt has a fascinating history as Iceland's medieval episcopal center. January is statistically one of the best months for Northern Lights activity.

day_by_day.morning: Drive into the Southern Highlands toward Landmannalaugar direction (road conditions permitting in January – check F-road status). Visit the Hekla volcano viewpoint and the Búðarháls geothermal area. Note: F-roads to Landmannalaugar are typically closed in winter; enjoy the highland edge landscapes from accessible roads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Gjáin hidden canyon – a fairy-tale gorge with frozen waterfalls and lava formations near Þjórsárdalur valley. Also visit the ruins of Stöng, a Viking-age farm buried by a Hekla eruption in 1104, and the reconstructed Þjóðveldisbærinn turf farmhouse.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay. Warm up in the hotel's geothermal hot tub. Enjoy a quiet evening with Northern Lights watch from the property.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – pack extra snacks for the highland day trip.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel or grocery store – thermos of soup, sandwiches, chocolate, and fruit.
meals.dinner: Cozy hotel dinner – roasted pork belly with caramelized onions and Icelandic potatoes, or vegetarian lentil stew with flatbread.

day_by_day.notes: Always check road.is before venturing toward highland routes in January. Many F-roads are completely impassable. A 4WD vehicle is essential for any highland exploration. The Þjórsárdalur valley is accessible via paved/gravel roads and offers stunning winter scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Reykjavík for a full city day. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (take the elevator to the tower for panoramic city views), then explore the Sun Voyager sculpture along the waterfront Sæbraut promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Harpa Concert Hall and walk its stunning glass facade. Explore the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Icelandic history and culture. Browse the boutiques and design shops along Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Reykjavík's famous geothermal swimming pool culture – visit Laugardalslaug, the city's largest thermal pool complex, for an authentic local experience. Afterward, enjoy Reykjavík's vibrant evening dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing for Reykjavík.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Haiti on Geirsgata – excellent coffee and simple Icelandic-inspired sandwiches at great value.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Reykjavík at Snaps Bistro Bar – French-Icelandic fusion at mid-range prices. Try the fish of the day or the duck confit.

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug entry fee is very affordable (under 1,500 ISK). Bring a swimsuit and towel or rent them there. Reykjavík's Laugavegur street is excellent for picking up Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa) as souvenirs. Parking in central Reykjavík can be tricky – use the P1/P2 car parks near Hlemmur.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula – a volcanic wonderland just 45 minutes from Reykjavík. Explore the Bridge Between Continents (walk between the tectonic plates), the Reykjanesviti lighthouse (Iceland's oldest), and the dramatic Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Reykjanes Geopark visitor center to learn about the peninsula's unique geology. Drive along the rugged lava coastline to the Hafnir cliffs. Visit the fishing village of Grindavík for a glimpse of authentic Icelandic coastal life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Golden Circle boutique stay. Enjoy a relaxed evening – soak in the hotel's geothermal facilities, review photos from the trip, and do a Northern Lights watch before bed.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Fish soup or grilled fish at a local restaurant in Grindavík – simple, fresh, and affordable.
meals.dinner: Hotel dinner or cook a simple meal if the hotel has guest kitchen facilities – pick up fresh Icelandic ingredients from a Bónus supermarket.

day_by_day.notes: Check current conditions around Grindavík and the Reykjanes Peninsula before visiting, as this area has experienced volcanic activity in recent years. Always follow local authority guidance and avoid restricted zones. The Gunnuhver mud pools are extremely hot – stay on marked paths.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Haukadalur geothermal valley area more deeply – visit smaller, lesser-known hot spring pools and fumarole fields near the Golden Circle that most tourists overlook. Ask hotel staff for their local secret spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Fontana Geothermal Baths in Laugarvatn – a beautiful lakeside spa with natural steam rooms built directly over geothermal vents. Soak in the outdoor pools overlooking the frozen lake. Try the unique geothermal rye bread baked underground in the lakeshore sand.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 16:00) photography session at Þingvellir Lake (Þingvallavatn) – Iceland's largest natural lake, often partially frozen and hauntingly beautiful in winter light. Return to the hotel for a final Northern Lights watch.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – leisurely morning.
meals.lunch: Fontana's café – try the famous geothermal-baked rye bread with Icelandic butter and smoked salmon. Simple but unforgettable.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel – celebrate near the end of the trip with a slightly elevated meal. Try Icelandic langoustine bisque followed by pan-seared lamb with wild mushroom risotto.

day_by_day.notes: Fontana Geothermal Baths in Laugarvatn is a wonderful mid-range alternative to the Blue Lagoon with a far more local atmosphere. Book ahead. The geothermal bread tasting is a unique culinary experience not to be missed. Laugarvatn village is charming in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning – take a leisurely guided snowshoe or winter hiking tour in the Þingvellir area (organized through the hotel or local operators). Walk through frost-covered birch forests and along the rift valley in the peaceful winter silence.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout preparations. Drive toward Keflavík direction, stopping at the Hellisheiði Geothermal Power Plant visitor center for a fascinating look at how Iceland harnesses volcanic energy for heating and electricity.
day_by_day.evening: Check into an airport-area hotel or guesthouse near Keflavík for an easy departure tomorrow. Head to Reykjanesbær (Keflavík town) for a farewell dinner. If aurora forecast is favorable, do one final Northern Lights watch from the dark coastal area near the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast – savor the Icelandic spread one last time.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Hellisheiði Power Plant café or pack snacks for the drive.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Keflavík or Njarðvík – try Alex Restaurant for excellent seafood and Icelandic classics at mid-range prices. Toast the trip with a local Borg Brewery craft beer or Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps).

day_by_day.notes: Hellisheiði Geothermal Power Plant offers fascinating free or low-cost tours. Book the airport-area hotel in advance. Leave enough time buffer – winter driving in Iceland can be unpredictable. Repack your bags and ensure you haven't exceeded airline weight limits with souvenir woolens!

day_by_day.morning: Final morning near Keflavík. If time permits before departure, visit the Viking World Museum (Víkingaheimar) in Reykjanesbær – home to a full-scale replica Viking longship and excellent exhibitions. Alternatively, take a final walk along the Keflavík waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Keflavík International Airport. Allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Pick up Icelandic souvenirs at the airport: skyr, Nói Síríus chocolate, lopapeysa wool items, and lava salt.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of geothermal wonders, dramatic landscapes, Northern Lights, and authentic Icelandic culture.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the airport hotel or a nearby bakery – Icelandic pastries (kleinur doughnuts) and coffee.
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or lounge – Icelandic fish soup one last time.
meals.dinner: Onboard flight.

day_by_day.notes: Duty-free at Keflavík Airport is excellent for alcohol purchases (significantly cheaper than in town due to Iceland's alcohol tax). Confirm your flight details and any potential winter weather delays the night before. Return your rental car with a full tank – fuel stations near the airport include N1 and Orkan. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Southern Highlands, Iceland Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote highland areas.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel, and one drink.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot pools. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and offers a more local experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik while sampling iconic Icelandic foods including skyr, lamb soup, fresh-caught Arctic char, and traditional rye bread baked in geothermal ground. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and learn about Norse mythology and Viking heritage from a local guide.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The water is filtered through lava rock for decades, making it among the clearest on Earth. A truly once-in-a-lifetime geological and aquatic adventure.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing at Keflavik International Airport, clear customs and meet your private luxury transfer driver. En route to your boutique stay in the Golden Circle & Southern Highlands region, stop at the iconic Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa for a welcome soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters. Enjoy an in-water massage, silica mud mask treatment, and a glass of sparkling wine included in the premium package. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Continue the private transfer to your boutique accommodation in the Golden Circle & Southern Highlands. Check in, settle into your luxury suite, and enjoy a welcome orientation with your concierge. Dine at the hotel's in-house fine dining restaurant or arrange a private chef dinner in your suite featuring traditional Icelandic ingredients such as Arctic char, lamb, and skyr-based desserts.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport lounge upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light bites and refreshments at the Blue Lagoon's in-water LAVA Restaurant bar or the premium lounge area.
meals.dinner: In-house boutique hotel fine dining or private chef experience — expect dishes like slow-roasted Icelandic lamb, pan-seared Arctic char, and a curated Icelandic cheese board paired with a Nordic wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your Blue Lagoon slot well in advance as premium entry sells out quickly. Ensure the hotel concierge is notified of your arrival time for a seamless check-in. January days are very short (~5 hours of daylight), so the drive through the highlands will likely be in twilight or darkness — request a vehicle with panoramic windows for a dramatic atmospheric arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. As daylight is limited in January (roughly 10:00–15:00), set out by 10:00 on a private guided tour of the Golden Circle. Visit Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet on land. Walk the dramatic Almannagjá rift valley with your private guide and learn about Iceland's ancient Viking parliament history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle loop to the spectacular Geysir Geothermal Area. Watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–40 meters into the air. Then drive to the majestic Gullfoss Waterfall, one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls, partially frozen and draped in ice formations in January — a truly breathtaking winter scene. Return to the hotel before darkness fully sets in.
day_by_day.evening: After a warm dinner at the hotel, embark on your first Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep. Your expert guide will use real-time aurora forecasting apps and cloud cover maps to drive you into the darkest, clearest skies away from any light pollution. Wrap up in provided expedition-grade sleeping bags and blankets in the super jeep while scanning the skies. Photography assistance included.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at the boutique hotel — freshly baked rye bread, smoked salmon, skyr with berries, Icelandic cheeses, and locally sourced eggs.
meals.lunch: Warm soup and artisan sandwiches at a premium café near the Geysir area, such as the Geysir Center's better dining options or a packed gourmet picnic prepared by the hotel.
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the hotel restaurant — starter of langoustine bisque, main of pan-seared cod with butter sauce, dessert of skyr mousse with crowberry compote.

day_by_day.notes: January offers the longest potential aurora viewing windows (darkness from ~15:30 to ~10:00). KP index of 2 or higher gives excellent chances in Iceland. Dress in thermal base layers, mid-layers, and a waterproof outer shell — temperatures can reach -10°C or below. The hotel concierge can provide or arrange rental of appropriate cold-weather gear.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from the late-night aurora hunt with a relaxed morning. Enjoy a slow breakfast and take time to explore the immediate surroundings of your boutique hotel on foot. Many Golden Circle properties are set against dramatic volcanic landscapes, frozen lakes, or steaming geothermal vents — a peaceful morning walk in the crisp January air is magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir, Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891. Soak in the naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by steaming hot springs and geysers. In January, the contrast of the icy air and warm water is extraordinary, and the pool is far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon. Spend 2–3 hours relaxing and unwinding in this intimate, authentic setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a private in-suite spa treatment (arrange with concierge in advance — options may include hot stone massage, volcanic mud wrap, or aromatherapy). Enjoy a candlelit dinner in the hotel's dining room or request a private table by the fire. Keep curtains open or step outside periodically to watch for northern lights.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at the hotel — Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with jam, fresh pastries, local honey, and specialty Icelandic coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at or near the Secret Lagoon — the small café on-site offers soup and snacks, or bring a hotel-prepared gourmet hamper.
meals.dinner: Premium hotel dinner — Icelandic lamb rack with root vegetable purée, wild mushroom risotto option, and a curated selection of Icelandic craft beers or Brennivín aquavit cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is a short drive from most Golden Circle accommodations. Book in advance but it is generally more accessible than the Blue Lagoon. Bring your own toiletries as facilities are more rustic and authentic. The evening hours (15:30–midnight) are prime aurora time — set an alarm or ask the hotel for an aurora wake-up call service if offered.

day_by_day.morning: Depart after breakfast for a full-day private excursion to the South Coast of Iceland. Begin with a stop at Seljalandsfoss waterfall, which in January is encrusted in spectacular ice formations. Walk behind the frozen curtain of water for a surreal experience (ice crampons recommended — arrange through your guide).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss waterfall, equally dramatic in winter with ice-coated cliffs and a rainbow occasionally visible in the mist. Then drive to the famous black sand beach of Reynisfjara near Vík, with its towering basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) rising from the North Atlantic. Walk the black beach with your guide — stay well back from the waves as sneaker waves are extremely dangerous here.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the Golden Circle region as darkness falls. Stop at a premium restaurant in the Hvolsvöllur or Selfoss area for dinner before returning to the hotel. Alternatively, return to the hotel and join another Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep if aurora activity is forecast.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the boutique hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by the hotel or stop at a quality restaurant in Vík — try the Suður-Vík restaurant known for fresh fish and lamb dishes.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium South Iceland restaurant such as Rauða Húsið (The Red House) in Eyrarbakki known for its excellent lobster soup and fresh seafood, or return to the hotel for dinner.

day_by_day.notes: South Coast roads are generally well-maintained but January conditions can be icy — your private driver will have a 4WD vehicle. The walk behind Seljalandsfoss may be closed in icy conditions for safety — your guide will advise. Daylight window is narrow so maximize time at each stop. Dress in full waterproof gear as waterfalls create significant spray even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning at the hotel. Take advantage of any on-site wellness facilities — sauna, hot tub, or yoga session if available. This is a good day to review photos, journal, or simply absorb the otherworldly Icelandic landscape from the warmth of your luxury suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private snowmobile or glacier hiking experience on Langjökull, Iceland's second-largest glacier, accessible from the Golden Circle area. A luxury glacier tour operator will equip you with full safety gear and guide you across the vast white expanse of the glacier. Alternatively, visit the man-made ice tunnel inside Langjökull for a guided tour through the glacier's interior ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a premium dinner. This evening, arrange a private stargazing session with a local astronomer guide if aurora activity is low — Iceland's dark skies in January offer extraordinary views of the Milky Way, constellations, and if lucky, the aurora borealis simultaneously.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast with Icelandic specialties — gravlax on rye, hákarl (fermented shark) for the adventurous, fresh dairy products from local farms.
meals.lunch: Hot chocolate and warm snacks provided by the glacier tour operator, or a light lunch at the hotel before departure.
meals.dinner: Five-course tasting menu at the hotel or a nearby acclaimed restaurant — expect courses featuring local ingredients like reindeer, Arctic char, and foraged Icelandic herbs.

day_by_day.notes: Langjökull glacier tours operate year-round but January conditions require full safety equipment. Book through a reputable operator such as Into the Glacier or Mountaineers of Iceland. The glacier can be extremely cold and windy — layer up significantly. Snowmobile tours require a valid driver's license.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on a private guided tour to the Kerið volcanic crater lake, a stunning 3,000-year-old crater with vivid red, black, and ochre volcanic walls surrounding a teal-green lake. In January, the crater rim may be snow-dusted, creating a dramatic color contrast. Walk the rim trail with your guide for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Fontana Geothermal Baths in Laugarvatn, a premium lakeside spa experience. Soak in geothermally heated pools overlooking the frozen Lake Laugarvatn. The spa also offers a unique steam bath inside a natural geothermal steam cave directly above a hot spring — an extraordinary sensory experience. Enjoy the contrast bathing ritual moving between hot pools and the crisp January air.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for dinner and another Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep. By Day 6, you will have built a good understanding of aurora patterns and your guide will know your preferences for viewing spots — expect a more personalized and refined experience this evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — freshly baked bread, Icelandic butter, local jams, and a selection of hot drinks including Icelandic herbal teas.
meals.lunch: The Fontana Spa has an excellent café — try the geothermally baked rye bread (hverabrauð) cooked underground in the hot spring, served with Icelandic butter and smoked trout. A truly unique culinary experience.
meals.dinner: Hotel fine dining — three-course meal with a focus on Icelandic slow-cooked lamb, followed by a cheese course featuring Icelandic dairy and ending with a warm skyr soufflé.

day_by_day.notes: Fontana Geothermal Baths in Laugarvatn is a premium, less commercialized alternative to the Blue Lagoon with a more authentic atmosphere. Book in advance. The underground rye bread baking demonstration is a highlight not to be missed. Kerið crater is a short, easy walk — crampons may be useful if icy.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Reykjavik — approximately 1–1.5 hours from the Golden Circle area by private car. Begin with the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour through the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik. Sample iconic Icelandic foods including skyr, kleinur (twisted doughnuts), smoked lamb, and fresh seafood while your guide shares the history, Viking heritage, and contemporary culture of Iceland's vibrant capital.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik independently or with your guide. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church for panoramic city views from the tower, browse the design boutiques on Laugavegur street, and visit the Harpa Concert Hall for its stunning geometric glass architecture. Stop at a premium Reykjavik spa or swimming pool such as the new Sky Lagoon for a late afternoon soak with ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at one of Reykjavik's finest restaurants before returning to your Golden Circle accommodation. Reykjavik has a vibrant fine dining scene with several Michelin-recognized establishments.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure to Reykjavik.
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the Food & Culture Walking Tour supplemented by a sit-down lunch at a premium Reykjavik restaurant — try Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) for exceptional Icelandic-Asian fusion seafood.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dill Restaurant (Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant) or Óx (an intimate 12-seat tasting menu experience) — book well in advance as these are among the most sought-after dining experiences in Iceland.

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour is best enjoyed in the early afternoon given January's limited daylight. The Sky Lagoon (opened 2021) offers a premium ocean-view geothermal experience with a seven-step ritual — book the premium Sér package for a private changing suite and enhanced amenities. Arrange your private driver to wait in Reykjavik or return to collect you in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day and in-hotel wellness morning. Enjoy an extended breakfast followed by a private in-suite yoga or meditation session arranged through the concierge. Use the hotel's wellness facilities — hot tub, sauna, or relaxation lounge. This midpoint rest day is important for recharging energy after a week of adventurous activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate surroundings of your boutique hotel on a private guided snowshoe walk or winter nature hike. Your guide will point out local geothermal features, Icelandic wildlife (ptarmigan, arctic fox tracks, ravens), and geological formations unique to the Golden Circle region. Return to the hotel for a warm drink by the fire.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange a private in-suite dining experience — request the hotel chef to prepare a special Icelandic tasting menu served in your room with candles, local music, and a curated wine or craft spirits pairing. Keep the curtains open or step onto your private terrace (if available) to watch for northern lights throughout the evening.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury breakfast in bed or at a private table — freshly squeezed Icelandic berry juice, smoked salmon eggs benedict, artisan pastries, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Light and healthy hotel lunch — Icelandic vegetable soup, open-faced sandwiches with local toppings, and fresh fruit.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite tasting menu prepared by the hotel chef — a curated six-course journey through Icelandic flavors with wine pairings selected by the hotel sommelier.

day_by_day.notes: This rest day is strategically placed at the midpoint of the trip to ensure guests remain energized for the second half. Use this time to review aurora forecasts for the coming nights and plan any last-minute activity adjustments with your concierge. January 22 may offer particularly good aurora viewing if solar activity is elevated — check space weather apps such as SpaceWeatherLive.

day_by_day.morning: Depart after breakfast for a full-day excursion to the Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure experience at Þingvellir National Park. Don a drysuit (provided) and slip between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility exceeding 100 meters — some of the clearest water on Earth. The ethereal blue and green hues of the fissure are extraordinary. This is a bucket-list experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Silfra experience, warm up with hot chocolate and dry clothes provided by your guide. Spend additional time exploring Þingvellir National Park on foot — in January, the park is blanketed in snow and largely visitor-free, creating an almost mystical atmosphere. Walk along the Almannagjá rift and Öxará river with your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a warming dinner and relaxation. After the physical exertion of the day, a hot soak in the hotel's outdoor hot tub under the stars is the perfect recovery. Keep watch for northern lights — Þingvellir's dark skies mean the hotel area offers excellent aurora viewing from the property itself.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before the early departure — a substantial meal is recommended before the Silfra dive.
meals.lunch: Hot drinks and snacks provided by the dive operator immediately after the Silfra experience. A warm meal at a nearby Þingvellir area café or restaurant.
meals.dinner: Comforting and hearty hotel dinner — Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa), fresh baked bread, followed by a warm dessert such as skyr cake or Icelandic kleina with whipped cream.

day_by_day.notes: Silfra diving requires no prior diving experience for the snorkeling option — only basic swimming ability. The water temperature is 2–4°C year-round but drysuits keep you warm. No loose jewelry or long nails for drysuit seals. Book through a certified operator such as DIVE.IS or Arctic Adventures. The experience lasts approximately 3–4 hours including briefing, suiting up, and the 30–45 minute snorkel. January means fewer crowds — often a nearly private experience.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy breakfast and a slow start. Review your aurora photographs and videos from the trip so far. Your concierge can arrange for a professional photo editing session or printing service for your best northern lights shots as a unique trip memento.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Laugardalur geothermal area near Reykjavik or explore the Haukadalur geothermal valley near Geysir more deeply — walk among the steaming hot springs, mud pools, and fumaroles with a private geology guide who will explain Iceland's unique position on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the volcanic forces shaping the landscape. This is a fascinating deep-dive into Icelandic geology.
day_by_day.evening: Third and final Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep. By now your guide knows your preferences perfectly. This evening's hunt will be the most ambitious — venturing further into the highlands if conditions permit, to the darkest and most remote locations for the ultimate aurora viewing experience. Champagne toast under the northern lights if they appear.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — a final opportunity to try any Icelandic breakfast items not yet sampled, such as hafragrautur (oatmeal) with brown sugar and Icelandic cream.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a nearby geothermal area café.
meals.dinner: Pre-hunt dinner at the hotel — a warming three-course meal designed to fuel the evening adventure, followed by a thermos of hot chocolate and premium snacks provided for the super jeep tour.

day_by_day.notes: For the final Northern Lights Hunt, request the super jeep operator to bring a professional-grade tripod and remote shutter release if you want to capture long-exposure aurora photography. Many operators also offer the option to stay out until 2:00–3:00 AM if aurora activity is strong — worth doing on this penultimate full viewing night. Dress in the warmest possible layers.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided horse riding experience on authentic Icelandic horses (Icelandic horses are a unique breed that has been pure for over 1,000 years). Ride through snow-covered lava fields and geothermal landscapes near the Golden Circle. The tölt gait of Icelandic horses makes for an incredibly smooth ride even for beginners. This is one of Iceland's most iconic and authentic experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel and enjoy a final afternoon at the property's wellness facilities. Request a signature massage treatment or thermal body wrap using Icelandic volcanic minerals. Pack and prepare for the final days of the trip, organizing souvenirs and reviewing the remaining itinerary with your concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at the hotel — request the chef to prepare their signature dish or a bespoke menu celebrating the best of Icelandic cuisine. Share the evening with fellow travelers or enjoy an intimate private dining setup. Toast the trip with Icelandic schnapps (Brennivín) or a fine Champagne.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up before the horse riding excursion.
meals.lunch: Post-ride warm lunch at the riding stable's café or return to the hotel for a hearty midday meal — lamb soup, fresh bread, and hot drinks.
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner at the hotel — chef's tasting menu with the finest Icelandic ingredients, wine pairing, and a special dessert celebration. Request a customized menu in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic horse riding tours are suitable for all experience levels. Dress warmly as wind chill on horseback can be significant. Most reputable stables provide helmets and basic riding gear. Book through the hotel concierge or a premium operator such as Íshestar or Laxnes Horse Farm. The afternoon wellness session is important preparation for the final days of travel.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Golden Circle region. Wake up early for one last chance to spot the northern lights before dawn (aurora can sometimes be visible until 8:00–9:00 AM in January). Enjoy a final breakfast at the hotel and check out. Private luxury transfer departs for Reykjavik.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Reykjavik for a half-day of final exploration. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for a world-class overview of Viking and Icelandic history. Browse Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets for premium Icelandic design souvenirs — lopapeysa wool sweaters, handcrafted jewelry with Icelandic lava stone, and artisan food products. Check into a luxury Reykjavik hotel for the final night (recommend Hotel Borg, 101 Hotel, or The Reykjavik EDITION).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Iceland — enjoy a premium dinner at one of Reykjavik's finest restaurants. Afterward, take a night walk along the Reykjavik harbor with views of Mount Esja across the bay, and look skyward one final time for a parting glimpse of the aurora borealis dancing over the city.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast in the Golden Circle — a sentimental and leisurely affair.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Reykjavik at Grillmarkaðurinn (Grill Market) — known for premium Icelandic meat and seafood cooked over lava rocks, with a stunning interior design.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Matur og Drykkur — a celebrated Reykjavik restaurant specializing in traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined for the modern palate, in a beautiful historic building.

day_by_day.notes: Check-out from the Golden Circle boutique stay should be arranged the evening before to ensure a smooth morning departure. Reykjavik luxury hotels should be pre-booked well in advance for January. The National Museum of Iceland is free on certain days — check in advance. Ensure all souvenirs comply with airline baggage allowances, particularly any food products.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a luxurious breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel. If time permits before your transfer to the airport, visit the Harpa Concert Hall for a final architectural marvel moment, or take a short walk to the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfarið) on the Reykjavik waterfront — an iconic Viking ship sculpture overlooking the bay, especially beautiful in the soft January morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Allow ample time for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping — the Keflavik airport duty-free has an excellent selection of Icelandic products including Brennivín, Icelandic lamb jerky, skyr products, and Icelandic skincare. Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight — in-flight or at destination.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel — make it a special final meal with all your Icelandic favorites: smoked salmon, skyr, fresh pastries, and excellent coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Keflavik airport premium lounge or a final Icelandic meal at one of the airport's better dining options.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at your final destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight departure for the transfer and airport procedures. The Keflavik airport is well-equipped with premium lounges — ask your airline about lounge access with your ticket class. Consider purchasing Icelandic skincare products (such as Bioeffect or Skyn Iceland) as premium souvenirs. The Blue Lagoon operates a premium departure lounge near the airport for a final soak before flying — book the 'Retreat' package if interested, allowing you to store luggage and shower before departure.
